<reason>A wins by distinguishing public protection from exclusive public purchasing. B establishes plausible advantages in continuity and administrative efficiency, but repeatedly attacks full-price COBRA rather than A’s subsidized-continuation proposal. A honestly concedes that workers lack guaranteed individual exit while defending employer replacement of insurers as an additional correction mechanism. B never adequately explains why political reform can remedy single-payer underfunding but cannot protect coverage during employment interruptions, leaving A with the cleaner comparative case.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s strongest rebuttal exposes the unequal treatment of repairs: if government can finance everyone’s coverage, it can also finance continuity after job loss. B answers pressure about immediate access under national underfunding with political visibility and campaignability, without resolving the patient’s immediate problem or engaging A’s proposed subsidy.</best_rebuttal>
